messages:
Maya (Sales): Heads-up — QuantumShield POC kicks off next week. Security & infra callouts: they need SSO (SAML) + SCIM bulk imports + RBAC. Two immediate blockers we flagged: 1) they send multiple NameIDs from their IdP (aliasing across apps) and 2) they expect SCIM bulk replace semantics for 50k users at ~400 req/s. Also pricing question: Hosted vs Dedicated for this pattern. Can eng/security advise? @Rach @Kyle

Rach (SE): Quick q — are those multiple NameIDs persistent (same issuer, different subject) or from different issuers? Behavior differs. If they come from the same IdP we can map claims; across issuers we need alias table.

Tom (Eng): We support aliasing via our idmap service today: we dedupe on (idp.issuer, idp.subject) -> user_id and allow alias bindings. If they present truly distinct issuer tuples, we'll create an alias entry and mark for admin verification. For SCIM bulk we recommend chunking — full replace across 50k is heavy. Example pipeline call we use for bulk import:
```
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/api/v1/bulk-import \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ingest-token>' \n  -F file=@users.csv
```
This feeds to a staging queue and applies idempotent upserts.

Kyle (Security): Couple notes: their ask for SCIM replace + high throughput + token rotation (hourly) is doable but we need to verify their token rotation flow. Hosted customers can do this but for throughput + audit separation we often recommend Dedicated. Also they want encryption key control (bring-your-own-kms) and longer retention of audit logs — flagging as likely Private requirement if legal insists on HSM.

Jen (Prospect): To clarify, IdP is Azure AD for most users plus a homegrown SAML proxy for contractors — proxy issues explain multiple NameIDs. We'll do a trial import of 50k users and hit SCIM at ~400 req/s for sync windows. Pricing: hosted looks expensive for continuous 400 rps — what committed monthly looks like for Dedicated?

Maya (Sales): Sales asks for a ballpark Dedicated commit for that sustained throughput so we can position the quote. @Rach — any quick estimate?

Rach (SE): Ballpark: for sustained 400 req/s and 50k daily churn we'd recommend Dedicated tier with reserved pool + burst capacity (S1 class). Rough cost estimate: mid-five-figure/month committed depending on retention and SLA. I'll pull exact pricing from pricing-ops. Also note: enabling SCIM pagination + chunked import reduces steady-state request rate.

Tom (Eng): Engineering implementation notes for the POC: 1) enable `name_id_aliases: true` in customer config to accept multi-NameID mapping, 2) use the bulk-import endpoint above to feed CSVs, 3) for live SCIM sync use chunked PATCH with page size 500. Sample SCIM patch pattern:
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/123
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [{"op":"replace","path":"emails","value":[{"value":"u@example.com","primary":true}]}]
}
```
We'll add throttling on the endpoint to protect other tenants.

Kyle (Security): I'll draft answers for the security questionnaire: encryption at rest (AES-256), KMS integrations (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / BYO-KMS), audit logging retention, token rotation, and SCIM auth patterns. If they require HSM-backed keys or logical separation of logs, mark as Private deployment. Also need to check SCIM bearer token rotation compatibility with their proxy.

ci-bot: deploy-bot created ticket #POC-4521: "SCIM rate-limit bump + aliasing config for QuantumShield" assigned to eng-platform.

Maya (Sales): Thanks — can we sync Tue 10am PT? Jen will join. I’ll schedule a 30m call and attach the security questionnaire so Kyle can prefill.

Rach (SE): Sounds good. I'll capture the exact pricing bucket after pricing-ops response and drop links in this thread.

Tom (Eng): FYI — memory/perf note: if their contractor users hit different NameID formats we may see more alias churn; we'll add a short-lived cooldown job to avoid DB churn during POC.

Jen (Prospect): Great — looking forward. I'll share a sample CSV and an Okta/Azure metadata snapshot before the call.

Maya (Sales): Awesome — thread closed for now, will reopen after pricing-ops reply and Tue sync. :thumbsup:
